verdict: Oracle's cloud revenue surged 47% and its order backlog hit $638B, but the quarter also carried an $823M restructuring bill and $1.4B of interest on the debt funding the AI build-out; net income was $4.3B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted; up from $1.19 a year ago

segments.name: Cloud
segments.note: Cloud services and license support: infrastructure (OCI) revenue of $5.8B grew 93%, and cloud applications (SaaS) brought in $4.1B, up 10%.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Traditional software licenses and support — slowly shrinking as customers move to the cloud.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to enterprises — down 10% YoY despite the growth push.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Mostly severance and related costs from a major restructuring — up from just $83M a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $1,438M on Oracle's growing debt pile, partly offset by $675M of non-operating income.

takeaways.title: The backlog is the story
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — work customers have signed for but not yet received — jumped $85B in one quarter to $638B, up 363% year over year, on giant AI contracts, some of them prepaid.

takeaways.title: Cloud is now half the company
takeaways.text: Cloud revenue rose 47% to $9.9B — 52% of everything Oracle sells — while old-style software shrank 2%. Infrastructure (OCI) alone grew 93%.

takeaways.title: Growth is eating cash
takeaways.text: Free cash flow for fiscal 2026 was negative $23.7B — $32.0B of operating cash flow minus $55.7B spent on data centers and GPUs. Interest expense hit $1.4B in this quarter alone.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges of $823M — ten times the $83M of a year ago — mostly severance as Oracle reshaped its workforce.
Net income of $4,304M is before $81M of preferred-stock dividends; income available to common shareholders was $4,223M.
footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud and software', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue.
